newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai police arrest drugs suspect wanted by U.S.
newsitem.headline: Thai police arrest drugs suspect wanted by U.S.

text.p: Thai police said on Monday they had arrested a key heroin trafficker in the infamous Golden Triangle poppy-growing region who is also wanted in the United States.

Liu Wei Ming, 57, an ethnic Shan and lieutenant of former drug warlord Khun Sa, was detained at his house in the Golden Triangle, which straddles the borders of Thailand, Laos and Burma, over the weekend, police told a news conference here.
His arrest comes a month after another key drug suspect, Li Yung Chung, a Chinese national who was also wanted by a U.S. court on drug trafficking charges, jumped bail in Thailand.
"He (Liu) is among the top 10 in Khun Sa's drugs syndicate," Major General Nophadol Somboontrap, chief of the Narcotic Surpression Police, told Reuters.
Liu had been wanted in the United States since a New York court indicted him on heroin trafficking charges in 1995, police said.

The minister-counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Bangkok, Ralph Boyce, said Liu was wanted for involvement in the smuggling of 168 kg (370 lb) of heroin into New Orleans in August 1993 which U.S. police intercepted.
Liu, who was present at the news conference, told Reuters that he previously lived in the Golden Triangle at Khun Sa's former headquarters. He refused to discuss drugs.
The half-Shan-half Chinese Khun Sa, 64, now lives in Burma under government supervision after surrendering to the Burmese military in January 1996.
The Golden Triangle is said by U.S. drug enforcement officials to produce about 60 percent of the world's opium, the raw material used to produce heroin.
Nophadol said 31 suspects had been arrested since late 1994, when Thailand and the United States launched an operation called "Tiger Trap" against drug suspects wanted by U.S. courts.
Nine had been extradited to the United States, one had jumped bail and the rest were in the process of being extradited.
Li Yung Chung, known also as Pongsak Rogjanasakul in Thai, jumped bail.
He was indicted by a New York court in May 1996 in connection with the largest heroin haul ever in the United States -- 486 kg (1,070 lb), in Hayward, California, in 1991.
He was arrested by Thai police last year and released on five million baht ($192,308) bail on February 7.
Li failed to appeared in court on March 7. The judge who granted him bail is now under investigation by the Thai judiciary.
Rangoon has denied reports that Li has sought refuge in Burma.
